newsitem.title: UK: Tele-Comms Intl to back Flextech BBC deal.
newsitem.headline: Tele-Comms Intl to back Flextech BBC deal.

text.p: Tele-Communications International Inc, the U.S. shareholder in Flextech, has agreed to back the UK satellite cable broadcaster in its main pay-television deal with BBC Worldwide Ltd.
The U.S. group will fulfil Flextech's financial obligations to the principal joint venture "in certain circumstances" if Flextech fails to do so, Flextech said in a statement.
Flextech will contribute 22 million pounds of equity finance, will make available a credit facility of 88 million pounds and a standby credit facility of 30 million pounds to the main joint venture.
It has also agreed to make available funding of 10 million pounds to the second joint venture.

Flextech's principal BBC venture will develop and launch, mainly in digital format, a number of new subscription television channels in the UK, Channel Islands, the Isle of Man and the Irish Republic.

The second joint venture will acquire and develop in analogue and, in due course, in digital formats what is currently UK Gold, one of the most successful channels on a British Sky Broadcasting 's multi-channel package. The deals are subject to shareholder approval.
TINTA's subsidiary UAEH owns 50.9 percent of the voting rights in Flextech, representing 46.5 percent of the group's issued share capital.
After completion of two joint ventures with BBC Worldwide, UAEH will hold 36.1 percent of Flextech's shares.
